text:
[RTIM.14.10] **The loader's skip-don't-reject does not discharge [RTIM.14.9],
and cannot.** The `Test*` / `Oracle*` family is additive metadata: a runtime that does
not run tests skips it and **must not** reject a bundle on its presence
([RDSC.9.4]), and it needs no release of its own to carry them
([LDET.1.10]). Both are correct for a production runtime, which has no
business refusing a program because it carries assertions it will never read.

They are wrong for a test interpreter, and the obligation therefore splits by
**consumer** rather than by atom. A skipped assertion in production is inert; a
skipped assertion in a test run is a case reporting success over a check that
did not happen.

The consequence to note is that **the version series is not the guard here.**
For every other wire extension a reader outside the series refuses the bundle;
because this family is deliberately skippable, such a reader instead runs a
weaker test silently — an unknown modifier on a known head
degrades to the head's bare meaning, and an unknown head vanishes. [RTIM.14.9]
is the only thing standing where the ladder normally stands.
